sub.en: Look at the sentences. Where do just and already go — and where does yet go?

items.q: I’ve ___ heard — she got the job!
items.why: just and already sit between have and the past participle. yet goes at the end, and only in negatives and questions.

items.q: I’ve ___ told everybody in the office.
She ___ the job on Tuesday. (a finished day)
items.why: RECYCLED from Lesson 17: a finished time takes the Past Simple.

acts.title: Four pieces of news, one group chat
text: AIGUL, 09:14 — Guess what! I’ve just heard from the school. Dana has got the place. She hasn’t told her father yet, so nobody say anything until tonight.
MARAT, 09:16 — That’s fantastic news! Congratulations to her. Has she seen the letter yet, or did they phone?
AIGUL, 09:17 — They phoned at eight. The letter hasn’t arrived yet, but they said it’s coming this week.
BEKZAT, 14:02 — I’ve got bad news, I’m afraid. They’ve cancelled the Saturday trip. Not enough people signed up.
DANA, 14:05 — Oh no! What a shame. We’ve already paid, haven’t we?
BEKZAT, 14:06 — We have, but I’ve already emailed them and they’ve promised a refund within ten days. Never mind — we’ll do it in the spring instead.
DANA, 14:07 — That’s something. Thanks for sorting it out so fast.

items.q: How did they hear from the school?

sub.en: These are the moves in a piece of news and its reply. Put them in order.

items.a: Give the news in one sentence
Say what has not happened yet
Say what you have already done

items.q: The two words Aigul uses to signal that news is coming.
The four words Bekzat uses to signal bad news.
The adverb that goes between have and the verb for something done before now.
The word that goes at the end of a negative or a question.
The three words Dana uses to react to the bad news.

items.sit: GIVING · You heard five minutes ago that your friend got the job.
o: Guess what! I’ve just heard she got the job.
Guess what! I just have heard she got the job.
Guess what! I hear she got the job just.

items.sit: GIVING · You want to know whether they have already been told.
o: Have you heard the news yet?
Have you heard the news already or not?
Did you hear the news yet?

items.sit: GIVING · You have bad news and you want to soften it.
o: I’ve got bad news, I’m afraid.
I have bad news, I fear it.
I’m afraid of bad news to tell.

items.sit: REACTING · Your friend says she has got engaged.
REACTING · Your friend says the trip has been cancelled.
REACTING · Small bad news, and you want to close it kindly.
o: Never mind — we’ll do it in the spring.
Never mind — we do it in the spring already.
Not mind — we’ll do it in the spring.

write.q: Write a short group chat: two pieces of news with replies, 8–10 messages. One piece of good news, one bad. Follow the model’s six moves, and use just, already and yet at least once each.
write.model: AIGUL 08:40 — Guess what! I’ve just heard from the university. Marat has got in. He hasn’t told anybody at work yet, so say nothing until Friday. — DANA 08:42 — That’s fantastic news! Congratulations to him. Has he replied to them yet? — AIGUL 08:43 — Not yet. He’s already written three versions of the email and deleted all of them. — MARAT 17:10 — I’ve got bad news, I’m afraid. They’ve cancelled the Thursday class. Not enough people. — DANA 17:12 — Oh no! What a shame. I’ve already paid for the whole term. — MARAT 17:13 — So have I, but I’ve emailed them and they’ve promised a refund. Never mind — we’ll start again in September.

speak.q: Give two pieces of news out loud — one good, one bad — using just, already and yet. Then react to these two: “I’ve just passed my driving test” and “They’ve cancelled our flight.”
speak.model: Guess what! I’ve just heard that my sister has got the job. She hasn’t told our parents yet. I’ve got bad news too — they’ve already cancelled Saturday. — That’s fantastic, congratulations! — Oh no, what a shame. Never mind.
